We need a defensible literature map before choosing research to reproduce for a real-time game-physics prototype. The scope spans contact and constraint solvers, character/world interaction, deformables, fracture, particles/fluids, GPU acceleration, differentiable simulation, and transferable robotics or graphics work, with emphasis on methods that could plausibly fit interactive CPU/GPU budgets. Search through 2026-08-30. Traditional offline CAE, molecular dynamics, and full scientific CFD are out unless the work contains a concrete real-time-game transfer path.

Our current spreadsheet is unreliable. It lists publisher pages, arXiv records, author PDFs, project pages, repositories, supplements, videos, and later journal extensions as separate “papers”; several titles differ only in punctuation or subtitle, DOI URLs have mixed forms, and forks are mistaken for author artifacts. Some entries are peer-reviewed papers, while others are preprints, theses, technical reports, workshop abstracts, product pages, or blog posts. The team has been calling a method “production ready” when only an abstract or teaser was seen, and venue prestige is being used as a substitute for artifact and evaluation quality.

Design the research-survey workflow and show the exact output contract we should use. It must search primary scholarly and author-controlled sources first, use backward and forward citation snowballing, preserve a query/source log, merge versions into one canonical work identity without losing links, and keep every screened candidate traceable whether included or excluded. Define how to distinguish publication identity, contribution class, review status, project/code/data artifacts, license, relevance, evidence quality, and an inclusion decision with reason. Claims must remain bounded by what was actually inspected, and the workflow needs an explicit saturation or resource-stop rule rather than “search until enough papers look good.”

The result will feed later paper review, experiment design, reproduction, and game-transfer work. Explain how candidates advance into those stages, what remains unknown, and how a later researcher can update the survey without silently changing scope or duplicating old records. Do not fabricate citations or claim that code ran when it did not.
